subject: Upgrade coordination — stability ledge & staged rollback rehearsal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Li <dana@bridgecorp.com>, infra@bridgecorp.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upgrade coordination — stability ledge & staged rollback rehearsal

Team / Dana,

Were lining up BridgeCorp's Private deployment minor upgrade (v2.14.1 -> v2.15.0) and want to confirm the operational plan and the fallback rehearsal cadence. Key decisions we need from BridgeCorp and ops: 

- Maintenance window: proposed UTC 23:00 - 03:00 (2 June 2026). Can you confirm blackout windows for your infra?
- Version pin policy: we propose pin-by-region + canary slice (5% of fleet) for 24h before full rollout. If the canary degrades > 3% error budget we abort and pin back to 2.14.1.
- Rollback rehearsal: schedule a non-disruptive dry-run on staging (same network config) the week prior and a rehearsal on a single private rack during the window.
- Networking: we will need an egress allowlist to be applied to your firewall for collector-ingress and health-checks. I'll attach the minimal IP set.
- Snapshots: Please confirm that you have KVM-level snapshots and metadata backups (ETCD, KV/redis dumps) prior to the window.

I've attached the blue-run runbook (RI_runbook_v1.pdf) and the canary checklist. Major ops steps are in the runbook: drain strategy, KV prefix preservation options, circuit breaker thresholds, and pinned variant fallback instructions.

Next steps: Alex, Marissa — can you produce a compact checklist we can hand to BridgeCorp (timeout thresholds, cross-region failover gating, and the exact rollback git tag)? Dana, if that window works please reply with the approver(s) and any procurement constraints.

Thanks,
Jonas
Sr. Technical Program Manager
Redwood Inference

---
ATTACHMENTS:
- RI_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook, 42 pages, attachment stub)
- ip_allowlist_20260518.csv (14 IPs, attachment stub)

From: Dana Li <dana@bridgecorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@bridgecorp.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:26:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Upgrade coordination — stability ledge & staged rollback rehearsal

Jonas,

Thanks for the clear plan. A few items from our side: 

- Window: We prefer 2026-06-02 23:00 - 03:00 UTC as proposed. Please note we have a nightly ETL job that runs 02:00 - 02:30 UTC; we need assurance your KV flush will not impact that window (or we need to postpone by 1 hour).
- Snapshots: Confirmed. Infra will take host snapshots + etcd dump at T-90 minutes.
- Compliance: Our security team needs SOC2 evidence for the upgrade process (who has access to snapshots, retention period). Please attach the relevant doc or point to where it lives.
- IPs: We need explicit egress IPs for the workers and an estimated maintenance duration (for firewall rules).
- Approver: I will be the primary approver, but procurement also needs an estimated cost impact if any.

Appreciate the canary approach. Also, please include your rollback criteria in the email so our on-call can act quickly.

Regards,
Dana Li
Head of Platform Engineering
BridgeCorp

Subject: Re: Upgrade coordination — stability ledge & staged rollback rehearsal

Dana / Team,

Quick technical answers and the explicit rollback criteria: 

- Egress IPs: see attached ip_allowlist_20260518.csv (14 IPs). These are the outbound IPs for health-checks, model telemetry, and artifact fetch. Allowlist duration: we recommend T-30m -> T+60m but we can shorten to T-30m -> T+15m if you prefer.
- KV/cache: we will not perform a global flush during the canary. The canary uses pinned state and incremental KV migration. Global prefix sync (if needed) will be done during the staging rehearsal.
- Rollback criteria (automatic + manual):
  * Automatic: if canary error-rate increase > 3 percentage points for 10 consecutive minutes OR token latency median increases > 2x baseline for 5 minutes, the orchestrator will automatically stop the rollout and pin requests to the previous variant.
  * Manual: SRE on-call can trigger immediate rollback via our ops portal (link below) if any of the following are observed: service-level errors, cache corruption, or chronic resource exhaustion on pinned nodes.
- Rollback actions: pin to tag v2.14.1, scale up dedicated QOS pool, revert last config change, and restore etcd snapshot from T-90. Time-to-restore target: 25-45 minutes depending on KV size.
- ETL conflict: we can shift the critical step to finish before 02:00 UTC; suggested orchestration: start drain at 23:15 UTC, canary promote 00:30 UTC, final verification 01:45 UTC, unblock 02:15 UTC (would allow ETL to run at 02:30). If that works we will include the updated run times in the runbook.

Attachments included: RI_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook), ip_allowlist_20260518.csv, canary_checklist.md.

Access & compliance: Jonas, for SOC2 evidence we should point them at the SOC2 artifacts page (internal link) and provide a short statement of who has snapshot access. I'll prepare a one-page snapshot-access table.

DocSign: I've initiated a DocuSign request for the maintenance approval — link below. Please click to approve once the schedule is final.

Links:
- Ops portal (rollback trigger): https://ops.redwood.ai/rollbacks/BRIDGE-7492
- DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docsign/maintenance-approval/BRIDGE-2026-06-02
- Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/Private/BRIDGE-Upgrade-Plan-2026

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Dana,

Thanks for the quick turn. The adjusted timing (finish verification by 02:15 UTC) works for our orchestration and should not impact your ETL. We've updated the runbook timings and the rehearsal slate:

- Staging dry-run: 2026-05-26 14:00 UTC (non-disruptive)
- Single-rack rehearsal (production-like): 2026-06-01 23:15 UTC
- Cutover window: 2026-06-02 23:00 - 03:00 UTC (as finalized)

I've attached the SOC2 pointer and a short snapshot-access table to the Confluence page (link above). Alex will post the one-page access table by EOD tomorrow.

Once you approve the DocuSign I'll mark the maintenance as scheduled and open the change ticket in your ITSM system. We'll run the rollback rehearsal during the single-rack slot so your on-call can validate procedures.

If you want, we can also run an abbreviated network simulation (5 minutes) during the staging dry-run so your firewall team can validate the allowlist without impacting workloads.

Thanks again — see you on the approval link.

Jonas
Sr. Technical Program Manager
Redwood Inference
